full_citation: E. Olsson, G. Chai, M. Dove, and Q. Cai, Adsorption and migration of alkali metals (Li, Na, and K) on pristine and defective graphene surfaces, Nanoscale 11, 5274-5284 (2019).
primary_claim_used: Pristine hollow-site values: Li -1.22 eV and 1.68 angstrom; Na -0.62 eV and 2.18 angstrom.
method_or_scope: VASP; PBE+D3(BJ); 4x4 pristine supercell; isolated neutral-atom reference; negative adsorption energy is favorable.
comparability_note: Closest quantitative benchmark for the pristine systems but differs in code cell size cutoffs and sampling.

full_citation: J. Cottom, Q. Cai, and E. Olsson, Vacancy enhanced Li, Na, and K clustering on graphene, Sustainable Energy & Fuels 9, 2813-2826 (2025).
primary_claim_used: Single-monovacancy binding energies: Li -3.23 eV and Na -2.52 eV; vacancy anchors both metals more strongly than pristine graphene.
method_or_scope: CP2K; spin-polarized PBE+D3(BJ); 308-site pristine supercell (307 C after creating one vacancy); 25 angstrom vacuum; Gamma point; isolated neutral-atom chemical potential.
comparability_note: Same functional and n=1 energy definition but a much larger cell and different basis code and sampling.

full_citation: O. V. Yazyev and L. Helm, Defect-induced magnetism in graphene, Physical Review B 75, 125408 (2007).
primary_claim_used: Monovacancy magnetic moments of 1.12-1.53 muB depending on vacancy concentration.
comparability_note: Supports the magnitude and finite-size sensitivity of the project C49 moment.

full_citation: H. Padmanabhan and B. R. K. Nanda, Intertwined lattice deformation and magnetism in monovacancy graphene, Physical Review B 93, 165403 (2016).
primary_claim_used: Planar monovacancy ground state with a 1.5 muB local moment and a competing nonplanar nonmagnetic state.
method_or_scope: Spin-polarized DFT study of competing vacancy structures.
comparability_note: Supports the magnetic planar solution while warning that a competing structural minimum exists.

full_citation: N. Dimakis et al., Li and Na Adsorption on Graphene and Graphene Oxide Examined by Density Functional Theory Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules and Electron Localization Function, Molecules 24, 754 (2019).
primary_claim_used: Carbon vacancies strengthen Li and Na adsorption relative to pristine graphene.
method_or_scope: Periodic DFT study of pristine defective and oxidized graphene across metal coverages.
comparability_note: Used only as qualitative trend support because coverage structures and dispersion treatment differ.
